thread:
Maria (DevEx): heads up — noticed some routing policy telemetry missing in the console after the py/ts SDK header rename landed this morning. dash shows lots of requests as `unknown_route` for a subset of clients. :eyes:
Alex (SDK): hmm, that sounds like our new `X-Rdr-Route` -> `Rdr-Route` normalization. we added strict header casing and dropped the prefixed header in v1.6.0. did you see any 4xx logs?
Maria (DevEx): no 4xx, requests look 200 but console metrics pipeline is treating route as absent. half the requests are from mobile clients on older sdk versions.
Sam (Eng-Platform): sending to @alex and @nora — platform still accepts both headers but mapping layer uses exact-match keys. we can relax matching on the ingest path for a short canary.
Alex (SDK): quick context: we renamed to conform with internal canonical header, but we included a fallback in the client only for TS; Python patch missed it. code we changed: ```py
# old
headers["X-Rdr-Route"] = route_id
# new
headers["Rdr-Route"] = route_id
# proposed fallback (quick fix)
if not headers.get("Rdr-Route"):
    headers["Rdr-Route"] = headers.get("X-Rdr-Route")
```
Nora (Console): console expects canonical route metadata at ingestion. if we tolerate both headers for 2 weeks, we need to update the dashboard tooltip and the attribution mapping so counts don't double. otherwise UX shows weird splits.
Kevin (Product): user impact? Are customers losing quotas or seeing billing surprises?
Maria (DevEx): two customers pinged support about weirdly high `unknown_route` rates; nothing billed incorrectly yet. quota enforcement uses route-derived bucket so could affect throttling in edge cases.
Sam (Eng-Platform): plan suggestion: 1) relax header canonicalization on ingest for 14d with sampling and a flag to re-enable strict mode; 2) patch py SDK with fallback within 24h and cut v1.6.1; 3) update console mapping to show "legacy header" tag in the next rollout; 4) notify customers via changelog + support playbook.
Alex (SDK): I can cut the python patch today. will add both fallback and a deprecated warning in logs so we can track who still sends old header.
Nora (Console): I'll add a telemetry mapping that coalesces both headers into the same route key and surface a small banner in the dashboard about the shim. also will add a hover tooltip explaining the timeline.
CI-Bot: deploy queued: platform/ingest-relax -> staging at 12:24 UTC, canary rollout 10% -> 50% -> 100% if green.
Maria (DevEx): thanks. can we make the canary opt-in by env flag so enterprise tenants can stay strict? some legal customers prefer exact matching.
Sam (Eng-Platform): yes, will gate by org-config flag and default to relaxed for new ingest nodes only. will log per-tenant fallback usage.
Kevin (Product): add a small blurb to the release notes and support article — "routing header rename: what to expect". also coordinate with account teams for customers with strict contracts.
Alex (SDK): milestone: patch release today, note in changelog, add telemetry hook that emits `route_header_fallback:true` for 1 week.
Maria (DevEx): i'll draft the support playbook and post it in #support after patch is cut. include example troubleshooting steps and `curl` snippets.
Nora (Console): one more ask: can we include a dashboard quick-filter for "legacy header traffic" so SREs can eyeball impact? small tile, yes/no.
Sam (Eng-Platform): yes will add a metric and expose filter. timeline: metric up in staging in ~3h, prod after canary.
Kevin (Product): ack. sounds like low severity but we need tight comms. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
Maria (DevEx): thanks all — i'll follow up with the support doc and a short customer-facing note.
CI-Bot: staging deploy succeeded at 12:37 UTC. monitoring checks green.
Alex (SDK): cut v1.6.1-patch at 13:05 UTC. pushing to PyPI and NPM.
Maria (DevEx): updating internal incident note and closing thread, will reopen if we see anomalies. :white_check_mark:
